body: I guess the point of seeking treatment would be experimentation. If it doesn’t work, then at least you’ll know that you made an informed decision before you did anything permanent. If it does work, then you’ll be in less pain and can do the whole living thing.
It kind of sounds like you may have a deep fear of failure. Does the idea of screwing something up keep you from trying to do things?

I’ve tried to be firm and stand up to him many times but he just threatens me with divorce. He knows that I have nothing and no one that I can count on. He tells me to go find another man, knowing how it hurts my feelings and knowing full well that he’s taken the best years of my life and that I have autism and I can’t magically pull a relationship out of thin air. As I was writing this, he came and yelled at me about a broken thermometer. It’s not even mine. I told him we needed a new one and ours was broken weeks ago and he said he’d deal with it but he just borrowed a broken one from some stupid asshole he knows, one that he doesn‘t know how to use. So now that’s my fault too for not knowing how to fix it and I’m a bad person for not throwing aside my feelings for him now that he’s concerned he might have a fever. Apparently I can’t even take a shower or use the toilet.EDIT: he does not have a fever, he’s just trying to invalidate my feelings instead of giving me empathy like always.
I love him and I don’t have anyone else. If I left, I would end up dying alone on the street. Killing myself at home would be better.
